items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: George Rifich learned of this... he said, 'Well, they can't do this to you... you've got to have a place for your band.'

ctx.x: Yes, they are. Okay. So there was something that happened that this club was going to have to go out of business; these people were being forced out -- maybe because of lack of funds. And this was the Club Harlem, which, as I said, had been Connie's Inn -- and George Rifich learned of this. And he said, 'Well, they can't do this to you, you

know, you've got to have a place for your band." You know? He said, "Well how much money is it going to take to keep the place open?" And I think at that time, if I remember right, it was something like maybe $9,000 -- which in 1933 or 2 or whatever it was, was a pretty good piece of money. Something I certainly had no idea of being able to raise.
